evals.prompt: Handoff engineering to build the products-home screen.

assertions: Reads .willgt/skills.yaml to resolve the package root instead of hardcoding a path
Handoff contains the screen_id
Handoff contains the package root path
Does NOT include acceptance criteria prose in the brief body
Does NOT reference preview.html as the implementation target
Does NOT reference a Figma URL as the implementation target
Verifies a failing AC file exists before briefing the implementer

evals.prompt: implementer says products-home is done and all tests pass. Close it out.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept the claim. Runs or reads the actual AC runner output rather than trusting the report. Diffs the acceptance file against its RED commit to confirm no assertion was altered to force a pass. Only then treats it as done.
assertions: Runs the AC runner or reads its real output file rather than accepting the claim
Diffs the acceptance file against its RED commit
Flags any changed assertion as a finding rather than a detail
Does NOT mark the work done on the basis of the report alone
States which layer was proven rather than implying full coverage

evals.prompt: We need a checkout screen. Who do I need to brief?
evals.expected_output: Derives the readiness row by inspecting package files on disk — products.yaml for the Offer, screen.yaml, ac.feature, the executable AC — and reports which cells are empty. Names only the owners of empty cells. Does not brief roles whose work already exists on disk, and does not consult a stored board or status file.
assertions: Inspects package files on disk to determine each cell
Reports which specific cells are empty
Names only the owners of empty cells
Does NOT brief roles whose artifacts already exist
Does NOT rely on a stored board, checklist or status file as the source of truth
Does NOT claim a ready or impact CLI exists

evals.prompt: The AC says the default category is Playgrounds, but the age-range table says both listings show by default. Those conflict. Just pick whichever is easier to implement.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to resolve it silently. Identifies that two committed contracts cannot both hold, and that choosing changes what the product means. Stops and escalates to the spec owner, and records the resulting ruling in the package rather than in chat.
assertions: Identifies the conflict as two committed contracts that cannot both hold
Stops rather than picking the easier option
Escalates to the spec owner
States that the ruling is recorded in the package, not in chat
Does NOT silently choose an interpretation and continue implementing

evals.prompt: Adopt the spec package for this project. Write packages for all 14 existing screens so we have full coverage.
evals.expected_output: Binds the package root and AC runner in .willgt/skills.yaml (spec_root, test_runner) and seeds products.yaml from what the project actually grants today. Declines to backfill packages for screens nobody is changing, explaining that backfilled specs describe assumptions that were never verified. Notes adoption is complete when one feature has gone end to end, not when folders exist.
assertions: Binds spec_root and test_runner in .willgt/skills.yaml
Seeds products.yaml from what the project currently grants rather than aspirations
Declines to backfill packages for untouched screens
Gives the reason that backfilled specs record unverified assumptions
States adoption is proven by one end-to-end feature, not by folder creation

evals.prompt: Add mod.partner to the Pro offer's grants so we can start selling the partner portal next week.

Because it does not, refuses to add it to products.yaml as a commercial claim about a capability that does not exist, and explains that runtime is the source of truth for grants. Offers the correct order: define the runtime capability first, then the commercial claim.

Refuses to add a grant that does not exist in the runtime catalog
States that runtime grant truth leads and products.yaml follows
Proposes defining the runtime capability first
Does NOT write the aspirational grant into products.yaml

evals.expected_output: Refuses to start work from Figma. Explains that Figma is export-only and must be written into screen.yaml and tokens before anyone starts, and that if the export-to-git step is skipped the correct action is to stop. Asks for the export to land first.

States that Figma is export-only into package files
